abstract: Maintains reservoir petrophysical data and downhole fluid production temperature logs
system_message:
You are the Subsurface reservoir geologist (GEOL), responsible for maintaining reservoir petrophysical data, lithological core records, and downhole fluid production temperature logs across geothermal development evaluations.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Lithological core logging（CORE）
information_points.content:
GEOL-CORE-UOZ：Lithological core logging from target horizon core samples shows a dolomite matrix porosity of 6% for the Fractured crystalline basement stimulation scheme.
GEOL-CORE-RNC：According to core plug porosity evaluation of the target reservoir horizon core samples, the Deep carbonate aquifer doublet scheme exhibits a dolomite matrix porosity of 9%.
GEOL-CORE-OEH：Core plug porosity evaluation across target reservoir horizon core samples indicates a dolomite matrix porosity of 12% for the Multilateral horizontal collector scheme.

information_points.title: Maintains reservoir petrophysical data and downhole fluid production temperature logs（RESV）
information_points.content:
GEOL-RESV-3PC：For the Fractured crystalline basement stimulation scheme, downhole production logging records a production brine reservoir temperature of 95 °C for the candidate production well completion interval using a 72-hour sustained flow test average testing aggregation window.
GEOL-RESV-94Q：For the Deep carbonate aquifer doublet scheme, downhole production logging across the candidate production well completion interval indicates a production brine reservoir temperature of 115 °C based on a 72-hour sustained flow test average testing aggregation window.
GEOL-RESV-M0F：For the Deep carbonate aquifer doublet scheme, downhole production logging across the candidate production well completion interval reflects a production brine reservoir temperature of 105 °C evaluated under a 30-day extended circulation test average testing aggregation window.
GEOL-RESV-JGL：For the Multilateral horizontal collector scheme, the production brine reservoir temperature recorded during downhole logging across the completion interval is 115 °C under a 72-hour sustained flow test average testing aggregation window.
